Extreme weather

Deep Freeze

A grid built for Texas heat is about to face a very different test. You have four years to prepare for the February 2021 freeze.

Play Deep Freeze↗ See what’s at stake ↓

The situation

Your starting point

You take over a public utility in 2017 with gas, coal, nuclear and wind power. The fleet looks substantial on paper. The question is how much of it will still work when heating demand rises and equipment freezes.

This scenario gives you advance warning of the 2021 freeze so you can try a different response. Spend on preparation, build additional supply, and leave enough money to run the utility through the emergency.

The choices

What will you do?

  1. 01

    Prepare before the forecast turns

    Compare winter protection with other uses for your cash. Work that is still on the drawing board cannot help during the freeze.

  2. 02

    Look beyond installed capacity

    Watch available supply as the temperature falls. Several sources can struggle at once, just as customers need more electricity.

  3. 03

    Keep service affordable

    New equipment has to be paid for. Find a way to strengthen the grid while keeping the public utility's finances and bills in view.

Put your plan to the test

What would you change if you could start preparing four years before the freeze?

Build, watch what happens, and try a different approach. The grid is yours to run.
